scope: initial Thailand-Burma advance through Allied withdrawal across Chindwin, May 1942

historical_anchors.early_detachment: Before the March-April reinforcement, an understrength tank company from the 2nd Tank Regiment made the long overland approach; secondary OOB reconstructions say only a small reinforced platoon reached Pegu after heavy breakdown attrition.
historical_anchors.Pegu_Payagyi: 7th Hussars records describe four Type95 destroyed plus another abandoned in one confused local action.
historical_anchors.reinforcements: US Army official history: 1st and 14th Tank Regiments arrived at Rangoon by sea during March-April.
historical_anchors.14th_regiment_scale: One contemporary-style OOB reconstruction gives 14th Tank Regiment 3 companies of 11 tanks + 3 HQ = 36 Type95 in 1942.
historical_anchors.Allied_armor: 7th Armoured Brigade arrived with about 115 M3 Stuarts.
historical_anchors.Allied_end_state: Museum/regimental history: about 45 Stuarts were lost to enemy action/mechanical causes during the retreat; roughly 70 remaining were then destroyed/abandoned at the Chindwin, only one being taken across.

early_overland_detachment_branch.combat_result: The extra reliability does not save this packet from Stuart overmatch; 4-7 are destroyed/abandoned/damaged in the Pegu phase. This is a canonical example of more sorties converting mechanical nonappearance into combat exposure.

main_reinforcement_branch.note: Exact 1st Regiment tank return remains open; 14th has the firmer ~36-tank anchor.

first_pass_outcome.Allied_Stuart_final_national_loss_delta: approximately 0; nearly the entire brigade tank park is lost/abandoned by campaign end anyway
first_pass_outcome.Allied_Stuart_enemy_action_share_delta: +5 to +9 tanks shifted from later abandonment/mechanical loss into earlier combat loss

captured_Stuarts.allocation: Primarily Burma theater/14th Tank Regiment experiment and replacement use; not free national production.

residual_by_mid_1942_working.1st_status: Still tied to Burma/redeployment pipeline; historically reassigned to Kwantung Army roughly four months after the March assignment.
residual_by_mid_1942_working.guard: These are first-pass residual bands, not yet regiment-by-regiment archival returns.

time_effect: More consistent Japanese armored pressure clears some roadblocks a few hours faster cumulatively, but does not prevent the Allied strategic withdrawal pattern or change the Chindwin end-state.
Bengal_link: The key downstream change is a somewhat healthier 14th Tank Regiment and a larger captured-Stuart pool in Burma. This does NOT automatically place a tank regiment at Chittagong; later theater allocation/terrain/road gates still apply.
